kurdistan-internal-security-forces-law-1.title: Scope of Application and Definition of Subject Persons (Statutory Jurisdiction)
kurdistan-internal-security-forces-law-1.conditions: The provisions of this law apply to all active-duty officers and personnel of the Internal Security Forces, as well as students of the Police College, institutes, and specialized training academies. It further extends to retired, dismissed, discharged, and resigned personnel if the offense was committed during and arising out of the performance of official duty, irrespective of any subsequent alteration in their administrative status.
kurdistan-internal-security-forces-law-1.penalties: Subjection of offenders to prosecution before the Internal Security Forces Courts and the uniform enforcement of statutory penalties across all designated categories without prejudice, ensuring the recovery of public and private rights accrued to the Ministry or victims.

kurdistan-internal-security-forces-law-2.title: Classification and Types of Statutory Penalties
kurdistan-internal-security-forces-law-2.conditions: Penalties applicable to the Internal Security Forces are categorized into three primary classes: Principal Penalties (Death Penalty, Life Imprisonment, Temporary Imprisonment, Detention, Dismissal from Service), Accessory and Supplementary Penalties (Deprivation of rights and privileges, forfeiture of medals and decorations), and Disciplinary and Administrative Penalties (Reprimand, salary deduction, room confinement, unit confinement, extra duties, extra training).
kurdistan-internal-security-forces-law-2.penalties: Determination of the jurisdictional scope of courts and commanding officers in imposing proportionate penalties commensurate with the gravity and peril of the felony, misdemeanor, or administrative infraction, coupled with the automatic statutory operation of accessory penalties upon the imposition of a principal sentence.

kurdistan-internal-security-forces-law-3.title: Felony of High Treason and Collaboration with the Enemy or Terrorist Organizations
kurdistan-internal-security-forces-law-3.conditions: Any officer or personnel who willfully aids the enemy or designated terrorist entities, divulges classified security intelligence and tactical defense plans of the Internal Security Forces, surrenders state-owned weaponry, munitions, or military assets to the enemy, or deserts post and flees during active combat or hostile engagement.
kurdistan-internal-security-forces-law-3.penalties: Imposition of the Death Penalty or Life Imprisonment, mandatory summary dismissal from military and security service, and total statutory forfeiture of all accrued financial rights and pension entitlements.

kurdistan-internal-security-forces-law-4.title: Felony of Mutiny and Armed Insurrection within Security Forces
kurdistan-internal-security-forces-law-4.conditions: The conspiracy or concerted assembly of two or more officers or personnel of the Security and Police Forces with the intent to mutiny against lawful command authority, or the deployment of armed force and violence to seize security headquarters or obstruct the execution of statutory duties during states of emergency or normal operations.
kurdistan-internal-security-forces-law-4.penalties: Imposition of the Death Penalty upon ringleaders and instigators of the mutiny, and Temporary Imprisonment (ranging from 5 to 15 years) for subordinate participants, accompanied by summary dismissal from service and forfeiture of pension entitlements.

kurdistan-internal-security-forces-law-5.title: Felony of Incitement to Mutiny and Subversion of Discipline
kurdistan-internal-security-forces-law-5.conditions: Any personnel or officer who disseminates propaganda or incites mutiny or disobedience to superior orders, or circulates false rumors and misleading reports within the ranks of the Internal Security Forces with the intent to demoralize personnel and undermine military and security discipline.
kurdistan-internal-security-forces-law-5.penalties: Imposition of Temporary Imprisonment for a term not exceeding 10 years during peacetime operations, subject to statutory escalation to Life Imprisonment or the Death Penalty if committed during wartime or active counter-terrorism operations.

iraqi-penal-code-1969-1.title: Principle of Legality of Crimes and Punishments (Nullum crimen, nulla poena sine lege)
iraqi-penal-code-1969-1.conditions: No act or omission shall constitute a criminal offense or be subject to punishment except by virtue of an explicit statutory provision in force at the time of its commission. Furthermore, no penalty or precautionary measure may be imposed unless expressly prescribed by law.
iraqi-penal-code-1969-1.penalties: Application of the statutory doctrine prohibiting retroactive or extra-statutory criminalization, whereby courts lack jurisdiction to impose unprescribed sanctions, mandating the dismissal of charges based on non-statutory acts and declaring the acquittal of the accused.

iraqi-penal-code-1969-2.title: Temporal Jurisdiction of Penal Law and Application of the Law Most Favorable to the Accused (Lex Mitior)
iraqi-penal-code-1969-2.conditions: A criminal offense is governed by the statute in force at the time of its commission, determined by the time the operative act was committed irrespective of when its consequence occurred. However, if one or more statutes are enacted after the commission of the offense and prior to the judgment becoming final and conclusive, the statute most favorable to the accused shall apply exclusively.
iraqi-penal-code-1969-2.penalties: If the subsequent enactment decriminalizes the act, the execution of the final sentence is immediately stayed and all associated penal consequences are extinguished. If the subsequent enactment merely reduces the statutory penalty, the court retains jurisdiction to review and reduce the sentence upon application by the convicted person or the Public Prosecution.

iraqi-penal-code-1969-3.title: Enforcement of Temporary Statutes
iraqi-penal-code-1969-3.conditions: If a statute enacted to criminalize an act or aggravate its punishment is limited to a specific duration or temporary emergency circumstance (such as wartime, state of emergency, or economic distress), the expiration of such period or cessation of the circumstance does not preclude the initiation of criminal prosecution or the execution of sentences imposed for offenses committed during its period of validity.
iraqi-penal-code-1969-3.penalties: Continued statutory accountability and enforcement of penal sanctions under the temporary statute despite its expiration, preventing offenders from evading legal accountability through the passage of time or the termination of emergency states.

iraqi-penal-code-1969-4.title: Territorial Jurisdiction of Penal Law (Principle of Territoriality)
iraqi-penal-code-1969-4.conditions: The provisions of this law apply to all offenses committed within the territorial boundaries of the Republic of Iraq. An offense is deemed committed within Iraq if any operative act constituting the offense is executed therein or if its criminal consequence occurs within Iraq, regardless of the offender's nationality whether Iraqi or foreign.
iraqi-penal-code-1969-4.penalties: Subjection of the offender to prosecution before Iraqi courts and the enforcement of statutory principal and accessory penalties, subject to recognized exceptions established under international conventions and diplomatic immunities.

iraqi-penal-code-1969-5.title: Jurisdiction over Vessels and Aircraft (Flag State and Territorial Waters)
iraqi-penal-code-1969-5.conditions: The provisions of this law apply to offenses committed aboard vessels and aircraft flying the Iraqi flag wherever located worldwide. It further applies to offenses committed aboard foreign vessels and aircraft situated within Iraqi airspace or territorial waters if the offense compromises state security or if either the offender or victim is a Republic of Iraq national.
iraqi-penal-code-1969-5.penalties: Vesting of exclusive or concurrent judicial jurisdiction in Iraqi courts to conduct investigations, prosecute, and impose statutory penal sentences against offenders in accordance with applicable statutory provisions without prejudice to public international law.

kri-peshmerga-ministry-law-2007-1.title: Definitions
kri-peshmerga-ministry-law-2007-1.conditions:
For the purposes of this Law, the following terms and expressions shall have the meanings assigned to them:
First: The Region: The Kurdistan Region - Iraq.
Second: The Ministry: The Ministry of Peshmerga in the Kurdistan Region - Iraq.
Third: The Minister: The Minister of Peshmerga in the Region.
Fourth: The Deputy Minister: The Deputy Minister of Peshmerga.
Fifth: The Secretary General: The Secretary General of the Ministry of Peshmerga.
Sixth: The Chief of Staff: The Chief of the General Staff of the Ministry of Peshmerga.
Seventh: The Council: The Defense Council of the Ministry.

kri-peshmerga-ministry-law-2007-2.title: Functions and Objectives of the Ministry
kri-peshmerga-ministry-law-2007-2.conditions:
The Ministry undertakes the following duties and responsibilities:
First: Protecting, guarding, and defending the Kurdistan Region and ensuring its national and supreme interests.
Second: Protecting the political entity of the Region and its democratic governing system, and preserving its constitutional institutions.
Third: Supporting the Federal Government in defending the sovereignty and security of Iraq pursuant to the Federal Constitution and the Regional Constitution, coordinating and cooperating with it in confronting security crises and disasters, and participating when necessary in war and combating terrorism in all its forms in coordination with the Federal Government.
Fourth: Establishing regular military formations and units and training them in all arts of combat and modern military sciences to qualify them for defending the Region.
Fifth: Formulating necessary plans for the development and modernization of Peshmerga forces, procuring all types of weapons, technical gear, equipment, and developing operational battlefield arts.
Sixth: Providing all matters relating to billeting, armaments, supplies, transportation, rations, salaries, financial and accounting affairs, healthcare, physical fitness, and general services for the forces.

kri-peshmerga-ministry-law-2007-3.title: Organizational Formations of the Ministry of Peshmerga
kri-peshmerga-ministry-law-2007-3.conditions:
The Ministry consists of the following formations:
First: The Minister: The supreme head of the Ministry and the primary official responsible for steering its policies, directing operations, and overseeing its overall activities.
Second: The Deputy Minister: Assists the Minister in managing the Ministry's affairs and exercises the powers delegated under internal bylaws or ministerial assignment.
Third: The Secretary General: Headed by a Secretary General with Special Grade rank, answerable to the Minister, supervising multiple general directorates including: General Directorate of Contracts, Procurement and Armaments; General Directorate of Personnel and Volunteers; General Directorate of Media, Morale Guidance and National Culture; General Directorate of Peshmerga Pension Affairs and Special Needs Care; General Directorate of Budget and Programs (Military Accounting); and the Legal Department and Military Courts.
Fourth: The Inspectorate General: Headed by a senior military officer, tasked with inspection and performance oversight of all formations, units, and facilities of the Ministry.
Fifth: Financial Audit Department: Undertakes financial oversight, audit of accounts, and compliance with statutory financial regulations.
Sixth: Directorate of Coordination and Relations: Regulates relations with relevant civilian and military governmental authorities.
Seventh: The Presidency of the General Staff: Headed by a Staff Officer with deputy chiefs for Operations and Administration/Logistics; comprising directorates of Operations, Planning and Modernization, Military Training, Signals and Communications, Organization, Combat Arms, Logistics and Quartermaster, Military Medical Services, Central Depots, Military Works, and Garrisons.
Eighth: Formations of the Regional Guard (Zeravani): Regulated by a special government regulation.
Ninth: General Directorate of Intelligence: Tasked with military intelligence collection, tactical and strategic security, and facility defense.
Tenth: Reserve Forces Command: Regulated by bylaw.
Eleventh: Ministry Defense Council: Composed of: The Minister (Chairman), Deputy Minister, Secretary General, Chief of Staff, Director General of Military Intelligence, Inspector General, and Commander of the Reserve Forces.

kri-peshmerga-ministry-law-2007-4.title: Executive Plans of the General Staff
kri-peshmerga-ministry-law-2007-4.conditions: The Presidency of the General Staff shall formulate the executive operational plans to achieve the goals and missions set forth in Article 2 of this Law, subject to the approval of the Minister.

kri-peshmerga-ministry-law-2007-5.title: Organizational Structure and Formation Bylaws
kri-peshmerga-ministry-law-2007-5.conditions: The Ministry may establish its organizational structure to fulfill its objectives in managing the Peshmerga forces; the duties, competences, and authorities of the Ministry's formations shall be prescribed by regulations issued by the Council of Ministers upon the proposal of the Minister.

kri-peshmerga-ministry-law-2007-6.title: Conferral of Military Ranks
kri-peshmerga-ministry-law-2007-6.conditions: The conferral and promotion of military ranks within the Peshmerga forces shall be governed in accordance with applicable military service legislation.

kri-peshmerga-ministry-law-2007-7.title: Ministerial Reorganization Powers and Instructions
kri-peshmerga-ministry-law-2007-7.conditions:
First: The Minister may, when necessary, establish, merge, or dissolve any directorate, department, or section within the Ministry's formations according to operational necessity.
Second: The Minister may issue the necessary instructions to facilitate the implementation of the provisions of this Law.

kri-peshmerga-ministry-law-2007-8.title: Repeal of Predecessor Legislation
kri-peshmerga-ministry-law-2007-8.conditions: Peshmerga Law No. (5) of 1992 is hereby repealed and replaced by this Law.

kri-peshmerga-ministry-law-2007-9.title: Supersession of Conflicting Provisions and Presidency Law Compliance
kri-peshmerga-ministry-law-2007-9.conditions: No legal provision or decision contrary to the provisions of this Law and Kurdistan Region Presidency Law No. (1) of 2005 as amended shall apply.

kri-peshmerga-ministry-law-2007-10.title: Executive Obligation
kri-peshmerga-ministry-law-2007-10.conditions: The Council of Ministers and relevant authorities must implement the provisions of this Law.

kri-peshmerga-ministry-law-2007-11.title: Effective Date and Gazette Publication
kri-peshmerga-ministry-law-2007-11.conditions: This Law shall enter into force from the date of its enactment and shall be published in the Official Gazette (Waqaei Kurdistan).

kri-peshmerga-honoring-law-2007-1.title: Legal Definitions
kri-peshmerga-honoring-law-2007-1.conditions:
For the purposes of this Law, the following terms shall have the meanings assigned to them:
First: The Revolution: The Kurdistan Liberation Revolution which commenced on September 11, 1961.
Second: Peshmerga (Regional Guard): Any individual who joined the Revolution and struggled politically or militarily for its goals, or subsequently enlisted in the ranks of the Peshmerga forces.
Third: Martyr: A Peshmerga who sacrificed his life during the Revolution in pursuit of the aspirations and freedom of the people of Kurdistan.
Fourth: Honoring: Moral and material recognition and valorization of the struggle and sacrifices made by the Peshmerga.

kri-peshmerga-honoring-law-2007-2.title: Coverage of Veterans of the Barzani Epic (1945-1958)
kri-peshmerga-honoring-law-2007-2.conditions: The provisions of this Law shall apply to all Peshmerga veterans who participated in the heroic Barzani epic march between the years 1945 and 1958.

kri-peshmerga-honoring-law-2007-3.title: Coverage of Liberation Movement Fighters up to March 5, 1991
kri-peshmerga-honoring-law-2007-3.conditions: The provisions of this Law shall apply to all Peshmerga who joined the Kurdistan Liberation Movement up to March 5, 1991 (the outbreak of the great Kurdish Uprising / Raperîn).

kri-peshmerga-honoring-law-2007-4.title: Medals, Decorations, and Honors
kri-peshmerga-honoring-law-2007-4.conditions: The classes, criteria, badges, and privileges of medals, decorations, and honors awarded to the Peshmerga shall be determined by special legislation.

kri-peshmerga-honoring-law-2007-5.title: Crediting Revolutionary Service as Actual Active Service
kri-peshmerga-honoring-law-2007-5.conditions: The period spent by a Peshmerga in the ranks of the Revolution shall be considered actual active service for the purposes of rank promotion, salary increment, and pension calculation.

kri-peshmerga-honoring-law-2007-6.title: Honoring Post-Uprising Martyrs and Disabled Personnel
kri-peshmerga-honoring-law-2007-6.conditions: The honoring of martyrs who fell in defense of the Revolution and disabled Peshmerga wounded following the date stipulated in Article 3 (after March 5, 1991) shall be executed pursuant to a dedicated regulation.

kri-peshmerga-honoring-law-2007-7.title: Issuance of Regulatory Instructions
kri-peshmerga-honoring-law-2007-7.conditions: The Minister of Peshmerga shall issue the necessary instructions to facilitate the implementation of the provisions of this Law.

kri-peshmerga-honoring-law-2007-8.title: Repeal of Law No. 9 of 1992
kri-peshmerga-honoring-law-2007-8.conditions: Peshmerga Honoring Law No. (9) of 1992 is hereby repealed and replaced by this Law.

kri-peshmerga-honoring-law-2007-9.title: Supersession of Inconsistent Decisions
kri-peshmerga-honoring-law-2007-9.conditions: No legal text or decision that contradicts the provisions of this Law shall be applicable.

kri-peshmerga-honoring-law-2007-10.title: Obligation of Implementation
kri-peshmerga-honoring-law-2007-10.conditions: The Council of Ministers and relevant authorities must implement the provisions of this Law.

kri-peshmerga-honoring-law-2007-11.title: Effective Date and Official Publication
kri-peshmerga-honoring-law-2007-11.conditions: This Law shall take effect from the date of its enactment and shall be published in the Official Gazette (Waqaei Kurdistan).

kri-peshmerga-disability-law-2007-1.title: Definition of Disabled Peshmerga
kri-peshmerga-disability-law-2007-1.conditions: A Disabled Peshmerga (Regional Guard) is defined as any member who, during the performance of duty or as a consequence thereof, sustains a permanent disability that impedes the continued performance of service.

kri-peshmerga-disability-law-2007-2.title: Conditions for Referral to Disability Retirement
kri-peshmerga-disability-law-2007-2.conditions:
A Peshmerga with permanent disability shall be referred to retirement in the following two circumstances:
First: If the degree of disability reaches fifty percent (50%) or above pursuant to a medical report issued by a competent military medical board.
Second: If the member loses an external bodily limb or organ (organically or functionally), regardless of the overall percentage of disability.

kri-peshmerga-disability-law-2007-3.title: Disability Pension, Battlefield Promotion, and Bonus
kri-peshmerga-disability-law-2007-3.conditions:
First: The disabled Peshmerga shall be granted a pension equal to the full last active salary and allowances received during active service, plus disability allowance commensurate with the certified disability rate.
Second: A Peshmerga who sustained disability in the field of battle at a rate of 50% or above shall be granted one higher rank, and his pension shall be computed on the basis of the new rank with honors bonuses.
Third: A Peshmerga sustaining 100% total disability in the field of battle shall be granted two higher ranks, and his pension and allowances shall be calculated according to the upgraded rank.
Fourth: A one-time lump-sum gratuity equal to the total salary received over the final eighteen (18) months shall be disbursed.
Fifth: A disabled Peshmerga who lost an external bodily organ under Article 2(Second) shall receive a limb-loss disability allowance of 50% of total salary.

kri-peshmerga-disability-law-2007-4.title: Disability Between 25% and 49%
kri-peshmerga-disability-law-2007-4.conditions: A disabled Peshmerga whose disability percentage ranges between 25% and 49% shall be reassigned to stationary units, or may elect upon personal application to be retired under the provisions of the Peshmerga Service and Retirement Law.

kri-peshmerga-disability-law-2007-5.title: Designation as Martyr Upon Decease
kri-peshmerga-disability-law-2007-5.conditions:
A disabled Peshmerga covered by this Law shall be designated as a Martyr upon death in the following manner:
First: If disability resulted from battlefield combat, the file shall be transferred to the Ministry of Martyrs and Anfal Affairs, and full salaries, allowances, and organ-loss stipends shall continue to be paid to the surviving dependents as received prior to death.
Second: If disability occurred during or due to service, the file shall be transferred to the Ministry of Martyrs and Anfal Affairs, and full salaries and allowances received prior to death shall be paid to surviving dependents.

kri-peshmerga-disability-law-2007-6.title: Living Amenities, Caretaker Allowance, and Medical Care
kri-peshmerga-disability-law-2007-6.conditions:
First: Competent institutions must provide living necessities and comfort accommodations suited to the disability of the Peshmerga.
Second: A personal attendant/caretaker shall be assigned for a Peshmerga with 100% full disability in cases of: complete paralysis, bilateral amputation above the knee, loss of both hands, complete blindness in both eyes, or post-injury schizophrenia/severe psychosis.
Third: The Kurdistan Regional Government shall bear full responsibility for medical treatment, prosthetics, and physical/social rehabilitation.
Fourth: The disability pension shall automatically be increased by any general increase applied to active serving personnel according to rank and grade.

kri-peshmerga-disability-law-2007-7.title: Statutory Privileges, Exemptions, and Housing
kri-peshmerga-disability-law-2007-7.conditions:
A disabled Peshmerga shall enjoy the following rights and privileges:
First: Free comprehensive healthcare across all medical institutions.
Second: A 30% reduction on public transport tickets inside and outside the Region across all carriers.
Third: Full exemption from statutory interest on governmental and bank loans granted to him.
Fourth: Free educational rights across all stages of study for the member, spouse, and children.
Fifth: Government commitment to allocate and secure suitable residential housing.

kri-peshmerga-disability-law-2007-8.title: Repeal of Law No. 7 of 2000
kri-peshmerga-disability-law-2007-8.conditions: Peshmerga Honoring Law No. (7) of 2000 is hereby repealed and superseded by this Law.

kri-peshmerga-disability-law-2007-9.title: Issuance of Bylaws and Executive Instructions
kri-peshmerga-disability-law-2007-9.conditions: The Council of Ministers and relevant ministries shall issue the necessary regulations and instructions to facilitate the execution of this Law.

kri-peshmerga-disability-law-2007-10.title: Non-Applicability of Conflicting Provisions
kri-peshmerga-disability-law-2007-10.conditions: Any legal text or administrative decision contradicting the provisions of this Law shall be void.

kri-peshmerga-disability-law-2007-11.title: Effective Date and Gazette Publication
kri-peshmerga-disability-law-2007-11.conditions: This Law shall come into effect from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette (Waqaei Kurdistan).

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-1.title: Legal Definitions
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-1.conditions:
The following terms and expressions shall have the meanings assigned to them:
1. The Region: The Kurdistan Region - Iraq.
2. Commander-in-Chief: Commander-in-Chief of Peshmerga Forces - Regional Guard.
3. Regional Government: The Kurdistan Regional Government.
4. General Command: The supreme authority of the armed formations of Kurdistan.
5. Peshmerga Forces: All armed components of the Kurdistan Regional Guard from private to general.
6. The Ministry: The Ministry of Peshmerga.
7. The Minister: The Minister of Peshmerga.
8. The Revolution: The stage of the Kurdistan Liberation Movement commencing September 11, 1961.
9. Peshmerga: Anyone who participated in the liberation revolution or enlisted in the Peshmerga forces.
10. Retiree: A Peshmerga entitled to statutory pension rights.
11. Pension: Monthly annuity disbursed upon retirement.
12. Salary: Final monthly base salary received according to rank and post.
13. Full Salary: Base salary plus statutory allowances.
14. Pension Rights: Statutory rights due to the retiree or heirs.
15. Pensionable Service: Creditable revolutionary, active, or authorized added service.
16. Peshmerga Service: Actual active service in the revolution or within Peshmerga formations.
17. Successor: Legal heir under personal status laws.
18. Beneficiary: Eligible dependent entitled to pension after decedent's demise.
19. Missing Person: A Peshmerga missing in action whose fate is unconfirmed.
20. Prisoner of War (POW): Captured by a hostile force during or due to duty.
21. Detainee: Captured or held hostage by an external or terrorist entity due to service.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-2.title: Appointment, Promotion, and Retirement of Officers
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-2.conditions:
First: Commissioning, resignation acceptance, retirement, and recall of officers from the rank of Lieutenant upwards shall be enacted upon the proposal of the Minister with the approval of the Commander-in-Chief.
Second: The Chief of Staff, deputies, division commanders, and special military command posts shall be appointed upon proposal of the General Command and approval of the Commander-in-Chief.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-3.title: Conditions for Commissioning as Lieutenant
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-3.conditions:
The qualifications for commissioning as Lieutenant in the Peshmerga forces are:
1. Must be a citizen of the Kurdistan Region.
2. Aged between 20 and 26 years.
3. Possessing good conduct and reputation, free from felony convictions or dishonorable misdemeanors.
4. Graduate of a recognized military college or 4-year higher education institution/university, or special Peshmerga command courses.
5. Physically fit and medically sound.
6. Age and degree requirements (2 & 4) do not apply to officers awarded ranks in honor of active revolutionary struggle.
7. Graduates of medical and engineering faculties shall be commissioned as First Lieutenants upon voluntary enlistment.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-4.title: Officers' Salaries and Annual Increments
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-4.conditions: The base salary and annual increment for commissioned officers shall be governed by statute.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-5.title: Time-in-Rank Promotion Periods for Officers

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-6.title: Conditions of Promotion, Discipline, and Leaves
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-6.conditions: Conditions governing promotions, accelerated seniority, disciplinary sanctions, and leave regimes shall be specified by legislation.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-7.title: Volunteer Peshmerga Enlistment
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-7.conditions:
First: A Volunteer Peshmerga is an enlisted volunteer serving from Private up to Chief Warrant Officer for a designated term.
Second: Enlistment, promotions, branch transfers, terminations, and retirements are executed pursuant to ministerial orders under regulations.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-8.title: Volunteer Enlistment Requirements
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-8.conditions:
Volunteer enlistment conditions require:
1. Regional citizenship.
2. Minimum age of 18.
3. Maximum age of 25 for technical corps and 30 for other branches.
4. Good moral conduct, without felony or dishonorable misdemeanor convictions.
5. Successful completion of sixth primary/basic grade.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-9.title: Volunteer Enlisted and NCO Hierarchy
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-9.conditions:
First: The volunteer rank structure spans: Chief Warrant Officer, Warrant Officer Grades 1 through 8, Sergeant Major, Sergeant, Corporal, Lance Corporal, and Private.
Second: Salaries and annual step increments are established by statute.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-1.title: Crediting Revolutionary and Combat Service
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-1.conditions:
First: Service in the liberation movement or Peshmerga ranks prior to this Law counts as active service for all pension, increment, seniority, and leave purposes upon verification.
Second: Pre-March 5, 1991 service and designated active combat operational deployments count double (2x) for pension purposes.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-1.title: Transfer to Civil Service and Service Portability
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-1.conditions: If a Peshmerga is appointed or transferred to a civil service post, all Peshmerga service years shall be credited to the new post for all civil service and retirement purposes.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-1.title: Contract Officers for Specialized Expertise
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-1.conditions:
First: The Minister may, with Commander-in-Chief approval, contract professionals as commissioned officers based on specialized technical requirements.
Second: Military rank for contract officers is granted upon ministerial proposal and presidential approval.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-1.title: Contract Term and Renewals
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-1.conditions:
First: Initial officer contract term is 10 years, renewable for 3-year increments upon ministerial approval.
Second: The officer is discharged upon contract expiration.
Third: In wartime and state of emergency, contracts may be compulsorily extended.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-1.title: Contract Cancellation for Misconduct
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-1.conditions: The Commander-in-Chief may terminate a contract officer upon recommendation of an investigative board for failure to maintain Peshmerga discipline and ethics.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-1.title: Secondment of Personnel
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-1.conditions:
First: Commissioned officers may be seconded outside Peshmerga formations for up to 3 years, renewable once.
Second: Enlisted volunteers may be seconded for up to 3 years, renewable once.
Third: Seconded personnel return to organic Peshmerga duty upon completion of term.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-1.title: Rights and Status During Secondment
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-1.conditions:
First: Secondment period counts as active military service qualifying for statutory promotions.
Second: Salaries and allowances are defrayed by the host receiving institution.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-1.title: Referral to Half-Pay Status
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-1.conditions:
The Minister may place an officer on half-pay list temporarily due to:
1. Misconduct reported through chain of command.
2. Professional incompetence and failure to perform duties.
3. Academic or operational failure in mandatory branch courses.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-1.title: Conditions Governing Half-Pay Status
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-1.conditions: An officer on half-pay receives 50% base salary and remains fully subject to military law and disciplinary obedience.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-1.title: Consequences of Half-Pay Repetition
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-1.conditions: Half-pay duration is deducted from creditable service on 1st offense, deducted doubled on 2nd offense, and causes mandatory retirement on 3rd offense.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-2.title: Military Chaplains and Imams
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-2.conditions:
First: Military Imams are appointed, promoted, retired, or recalled by ministerial order.
Second: Imams are governed by the same legal provisions applicable to officers of equivalent salary grades.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-2.title: Qualifications for Military Imams
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-2.conditions: Imam candidates must meet Article 3 requirements (except clause 4), possessing a bachelor's degree in Islamic/Sharia jurisprudence or equivalent.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-2.title: Imam Duties, Insignia, and Directives
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-2.conditions: Ministerial instructions shall prescribe the Imam's rank equivalent, salary increments, duties, uniform, and badges.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-2.title: Maternity Rights for Women Personnel
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-2.conditions: Female members serving in Peshmerga forces are entitled to full pay and all allowances throughout childbirth and statutory maternity leave.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-2.title: Advancement and Leave Rules
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-2.conditions: Progression rules, disciplinary penalties, leaves, and conditions for ranks are regulated under applicable military law.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-2.title: Statutory Retirement Age by Rank
General Command Retirement Authority
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-2.conditions:
The General Command may retire Peshmerga personnel in cases of:
1. Cadre surplus beyond approved staffing establishment.
2. Established operational incompetence.
3. Violation of Peshmerga ethical codes and institutional principles.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-2.title: Voluntary Retirement and Severance Below 15 Years
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-2.conditions:
First: A Peshmerga with at least 15 years creditable service may apply for voluntary retirement with ministerial consent.
Second: If retired with under 15 years service, a lump-sum severance gratuity of 200% of final monthly salary per completed year of service is disbursed.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-2.title: Pension Calculation Formula and Family Allowances
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-2.conditions:
First: The monthly pension is calculated by multiplying the last received salary by the number of completed pensionable months and dividing by 260.
Second: Monthly family allowances consist of 50,000 IQD for the spouse and 25,000 IQD per child for up to 5 children.
Third: Month and year fractions are rounded up to whole units.
Fourth: Under no circumstances may the pension exceed the final active salary.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-2.title: End-of-Service Gratuity
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-2.conditions:
First: End-of-service gratuity is granted upon retirement as follows:
1. One year's full active salary for 15+ years of pre-March 5, 1991 service.
2. One year's full active salary for 20+ years overall creditable service.
Second: In all other eligible retirement cases, a gratuity equal to 6 months final salary is awarded.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-3.title: Devolution of Rights to Surviving Heirs
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-3.conditions: Upon the death of a Peshmerga or pensioner, all pension entitlements, allowances, and accrued rights transfer to eligible statutory heirs.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-3.title: Effective Date of Pension Disbursement
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-3.conditions: Pensions commence from date of discharge or death; delayed applications exceeding 3 years without lawful cause commence from application filing date.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-3.title: Option Between Pension and Civil Salary
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-3.conditions: If a pensioner is re-employed in a public civil office, he may elect between receiving his pension or active employment salary.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-3.title: Missing and Detained Personnel
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-3.conditions:
First: When a Peshmerga is missing or captured in duty, full salary continues to dependent heirs until return or verified decease.
Second: Pension is granted to heirs upon certified death or after 2 years of missing status, transferring records to Ministry of Martyrs.
Third: In cases of negligent desertion or ethical misconduct, legal prosecution and disciplinary retirement follow.
Fourth: The duration of captivity or missing status counts as active service.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-3.title: Death and Martyrdom in the Line of Duty
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-3.conditions:
First: If a member dies in service with under 15 years service, creditable service is elevated to 15 years for full pension entitlement.
Second: Combat martyrs receive rights and honors under the Ministry of Martyrs and Anfal Affairs legislation.
Third: Pre-1991 continuous serving personnel are included.
Fourth: Files are transmitted to the Ministry of Martyrs.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-3.title: Rights of Prisoners of War (POWs)
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-3.conditions:
First: Full salary, allowances, and emoluments are paid to dependents throughout captivity.
Second: The period of enemy captivity counts as actual active military service for all purposes.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-3.title: Forfeiture of Pension for Treason
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-3.conditions: Pensioners or surviving heirs forfeit statutory pension entitlements upon established legal proof of treason or collaboration with hostile enemies of Kurdistan.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-3.title: Recall of Pensioners and Gratuity
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-3.conditions: If a retiree is recalled to military duty by General Command order, retirement severance gratuity shall not be disbursed twice.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-3.title: Prohibition of Dual Official Salaries
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-3.conditions: No individual drawing a statutory Peshmerga pension may concurrently receive another official government salary.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-3.title: Pre-1991 Veterans Credited to 15 Years
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-3.conditions: Veterans joining the revolution pre-1991 with at least 3 years service are retired with credited 15 years service subject to: no other state salary, never opposed the revolution, uninterrupted service, and minimum age 16 at enlistment.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-4.title: Automatic Parity with Active Pay Scales
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-4.conditions: Whenever active service pay scales are upgraded, pensions automatically adjust in equal percentage by rank and post.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-4.title: Assimilation of Existing Peshmerga Cadres
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-4.conditions: Personnel currently serving in Peshmerga forces are confirmed in their substantive ranks and entitled to full statutory retirement rights.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-4.title: Crediting Military College Studies
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-4.conditions: Graduation study periods in recognized military colleges/institutes count as creditable service for retirement purposes only.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-4.title: Non-Assignability and Seizure Limits
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-4.conditions:
First: Pension rights cannot be assigned or waived; any assignment is void ab initio.
Second: Attachment is barred except for court-ordered child/spousal support and debts due to Regional Treasury.
Third: In no case may attachment exceed 25% of monthly pension or gratuity.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-4.title: Service Extension for Senior Officers
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-4.conditions: The Commander-in-Chief may extend the active service of senior officers, technicians, and specialists for up to 2 years for compelling public interest.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-4.title: Exclusion of Former Regime Collaborators and War Criminals
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-4.conditions: This Law strictly excludes any individual legally proven to have collaborated with the repressive organs of the former regime or participated in Anfal and genocide crimes.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-4.title: Equality with Federal Armed Forces Standards
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-4.conditions: Peshmerga covered by this Law benefit from all rights, benefits, and privileges granted to counterparts in the federal Iraqi armed forces under federal law.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-4.title: Prohibition of Partisan Political Activities
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-4.conditions: Partisan political activities and organizing within the ranks and formations of the Peshmerga forces are strictly prohibited.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-4.title: Application to Kurdistan Citizens Outside the Region
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-4.conditions: Provisions of this Law extend to qualified citizens of Kurdistan residing outside the administrative boundaries of the Region.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-4.title: Supersession of Inconsistent Decisions
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-4.conditions: Any legal text, directive, or decision conflicting with the provisions of this Law is superseded and inapplicable.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-5.title: Cabinet Bylaw and Regulatory Mandate
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-5.conditions: The Council of Ministers and respective ministries are empowered to promulgate regulations and orders to execute this Law.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-5.title: Implementation Duty
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-5.conditions: The Council of Ministers and relevant governmental agencies must enforce and execute this Law.

kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-5.title: Effective Date and Official Gazette Publication
kri-peshmerga-service-pension-law-2007-5.conditions: This Law enters into force from the date of its enactment and shall be published in the Official Gazette (Waqaei Kurdistan).

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-1.title: Scope of Application and Military Definitions
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-1.conditions:
First: The provisions of this Code apply to:
a. Active personnel of the Iraqi Armed Forces for crimes committed during or resulting from duty.
b. Cadets of military colleges, institutes, and service academies.
c. Retired, dismissed, or discharged officers, warrant officers, NCOs, and soldiers for crimes committed during active service.
d. Prisoners of war regarding offenses committed in detention camps.
e. Active reserve officers, NCOs, and enlisted personnel.
Second: Statutory Definitions: Officer (Lieutenant and above, including military Imams); Warrant Officer (Grades); NCO (Sergeants and Corporals); Private/Soldier (All enlisted servicemen); Army (Land, Naval, and Air forces); Unit/Detachment (Any formation under command of an officer).

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-2.title: Mobilization and State of Readiness
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-2.conditions:
First: Mobilization is the call-up of all or part of the military reserves into active service during external aggression or active operations.
Second: Mobilization commences upon the issuance of a written executive decree placing forces on mobilization and terminates upon its revocation.
Third: Military aircraft and naval vessels departing Iraqi territory in peacetime are deemed in a state of mobilization until return to base.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-3.title: Offenses Committed Outside Iraq
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-3.conditions: Offenses covered under this Code committed by military personnel abroad while on deployed forces, official missions, or study assignments are deemed committed in Iraq if not prosecuted in the foreign jurisdiction.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-4.title: Prosecution of Prisoners of War under Geneva Conventions
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-4.conditions: Trials of prisoners of war before military tribunals shall proceed pursuant to the provisions of this Code and the Geneva Conventions relative to the Treatment of Prisoners of War.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-5.title: Crimes Against Allied Forces
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-5.conditions:
First: Offenses committed against servicemen of allied nations during joint operations are treated as if committed against Iraqi personnel, subject to reciprocal international agreements.
Second: A serviceman refers to any person pursuing military service as an occupation.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-6.title: Facing the Enemy
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-6.conditions: All military formations, aircraft, and naval combatants are deemed facing the enemy from the commencement of tactical preparations for mobilization and battle.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-7.title: Definitions of Enemy, Armed Status, Duty, and Commander
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-7.conditions:
Statutory Operational Terms:
First: Enemy: Any foreign state, hostile force, or armed insurgent group bearing arms against Iraq.
Second: Armed: Bearing arms for operational service or assembling armed under command.
Third: Duty/Service: Execution of specific military missions upon lawful superior orders.
Fourth: Commander: Person invested with command authority by law.
Fifth: Military Mutiny: Collective refusal to obey commands, violent resistance, or strike against military orders.
Sixth: Room Detention: Confinement of personnel inside dedicated quarters within camp limits.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-8.title: Aggravating Circumstance in Troop Assembly
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-8.conditions: An offense is deemed aggravated if committed in an assembly before at least three military persons assembled for official service, excluding principals and accomplices.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-9.title: Definitions of Sentry and Guard Detail
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-9.conditions:
First: Sentry: An armed military serviceman stationed at a designated post to preserve security, surveillance, and order in peace or war.
Second: Guard Detail (Patrol): One or more armed servicemen under command detailed for statutory security missions.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-10.title: Classification of Primary Penalties
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-10.conditions:
Primary statutory penalties comprise:
1. Execution: Capital punishment inflicted by firing squad.
2. Life Imprisonment: Confinement for a period of twenty years.
3. Temporary Imprisonment: Confinement from over 5 years up to 15 years.
4. Severe Confinement: Incarceration from over 3 months up to 5 years with hard labor.
5. Simple Confinement: Incarceration from 24 hours up to 3 years.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-11.title: Fines and Seniority Deduction for Officers
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-11.conditions: For offenses punishable by confinement not exceeding 3 years, an officer may be sentenced to a fine or loss of seniority not exceeding 2 years in lieu of imprisonment upon mitigating grounds, excluding dishonorable offenses.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-12.title: Barracks Confinement Rules and Limits
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-12.conditions: Barracks confinement may be imposed on officers for up to 15 days, and on warrant officers, NCOs, and privates for up to 30 days; it shall not be imposed on academy cadets.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-13.title: Regime of Barracks Confinement
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-13.conditions: Personnel sentenced to barracks confinement are not exempt from routine duty or field parade, are barred from leaving military premises, and cannot receive visitors except on service necessity.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-14.title: Salary Rights During Barracks Confinement
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-14.conditions: Personnel undergoing barracks confinement remain entitled to their full salaries and allowances during confinement.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-15.title: Mandatory and Discretionary Expulsion/Discharge
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-15.conditions:
First: Expulsion from service or contract annulment is mandatory upon conviction to death, life or temporary imprisonment, terrorism offenses, dishonorable crimes, or rape and sexual assaults.
Second: The military tribunal may discretionary order expulsion upon conviction to simple confinement.
Third: An officer shall be cashiered if he forfeits any mandatory condition of his appointment.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-16.title: Legal Consequences of Cashiering and Expulsion
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-16.conditions: Expulsion entails forfeiture of military rank, decorations, medals, and absolute lifetime disqualification from re-enlisting in the armed forces.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-17.title: Rank Reduction of NCOs and Warrant Officers
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-17.conditions: The tribunal may reduce a non-commissioned officer or warrant officer to a subordinate grade or to the rank of private for punishable offenses.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-18.title: Forfeiture of Commission and Rank
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-18.conditions: Forfeiture of rank deprives the officer of his commission and status, relegating him to civilian standing without military privileges.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-19.title: Salary Stoppages and Deductions
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-19.conditions: Deductions from pay may be awarded as a disciplinary sanction, not exceeding one-third (1/3) of monthly pay for the awarded term.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-20.title: Reprimand and Severe Reprimand
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-20.conditions: Reprimand and severe reprimand are entered in writing in the service record, legally retarding eligibility for promotion and step increases.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-21.title: Extra Guard and Drill Duties
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-21.conditions: Extra guard watch, fatigues, and disciplinary drills may be awarded to enlisted personnel pursuant to military command bylaws.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-22.title: Execution of Sentences in Military Prisons
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-22.conditions: Sentences of confinement are executed within military prisons and garrison detention centers pursuant to Ministry of Defense regulations.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-23.title: Deduction of Pre-Trial Remand from Sentence
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-23.conditions: Pre-trial detention and custody served prior to final judgment shall be fully deducted from the term of imprisonment imposed.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-24.title: Plurality of Offenses and Sentence Aggregation
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-24.conditions: Where multiple related offenses are committed, the tribunal imposes the penalty prescribed for the gravest offense unless cumulative execution is statutory.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-25.title: Mitigating and Aggravating Factors in Military Justice
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-25.conditions: Military tribunals evaluate valor in combat, prior disciplinary record, battlefield conditions, and aggravating or mitigating factors in sentencing.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-26.title: Prohibition of Suspended Sentences for Grave Offenses
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-26.conditions: Stay or suspension of sentence execution is barred for offenses of high treason, armed mutiny, desertion facing the enemy, or ammunition theft.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-27.title: High Treason and Bearing Arms Against the State
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-27.conditions: Capital punishment (death) applies to any serviceman who bears arms against Iraq or joins hostile enemy forces in time of war or mobilization.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-28.title: Surrender of Fortifications and Units to the Enemy
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-28.conditions: Death penalty applies to any commander who surrenders a fortress, position, vessel, or combat aircraft to the enemy without exhausting all defense.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-29.title: Espionage and Leaking Military Secrets
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-29.conditions: Death penalty applies to any serviceman engaging in espionage, intelligence disclosure, or delivering defense operational secrets to foreign powers.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-30.title: Demoralization and Spreading Panic During Operations
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-30.conditions: Punishable by death or life imprisonment: causing panic, defeatism, or inciting retreat among troops in the field facing the enemy.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-31.title: Sabotage of Military Installations and Defenses
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-31.conditions: Death penalty is incurred for intentional sabotage of military installations, communication links, supply lines, or ammunition dumps.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-32.title: Harboring Enemy Spies and Facilitating Escape
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-32.conditions: Punishable by life or temporary imprisonment: harboring, concealing, or aiding the escape of enemy spies or combatants.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-33.title: Illicit Commercial Dealing with the Enemy
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-33.conditions: Punishable by temporary imprisonment: conducting trade, supply transfers, or financial transactions with the enemy during war.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-34.title: Plundering Wounded and Deceased in Combat
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-34.conditions: Imprisonment up to 10 years for pillaging, stripping possessions, or robbing wounded soldiers or war dead on the battlefield.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-35.title: Failure of Commander to Relieve Besieged Friendly Forces
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-35.conditions: Death or life imprisonment for a commander who intentionally fails to relieve or support engaged friendly troops when capable of intervention.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-36.title: Military Mutiny in Peace and War
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-36.conditions: Capital punishment applies to ringleaders and inciters of mutiny facing the enemy; temporary imprisonment applies if mutiny occurs in peacetime.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-37.title: Incitement to Mutiny and Failure to Suppress Mutiny
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-37.conditions: Punishable by imprisonment: failure by an officer aware of a mutinous conspiracy to suppress it immediately or report it to higher headquarters.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-38.title: Refusal of Direct Lawful Orders During Operations
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-38.conditions: Imprisonment for not less than 7 years for refusing a direct lawful command relating to tactical field duties during operations or mobilization.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-39.title: Refusal of Lawful Orders in Peacetime
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-39.conditions: Severe confinement up to 3 years for intentionally disobeying a lawful command issued by a military superior in peacetime.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-40.title: Collective Unlawful Petitions and Grievances
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-40.conditions: Confinement up to 1 year for organizing, signing, or presenting collective grievances in violation of military service channels.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-41.title: Contempt and Desecration of National and Military Flags
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-41.conditions: Confinement up to 3 years for publicly insulting or showing contempt toward the national flag or armed forces emblems.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-42.title: Desertion to the Enemy
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-42.conditions: Mandatory capital punishment by firing squad applies to any serviceman who deserts to or crosses over to the enemy.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-43.title: Desertion in the Face of the Enemy
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-43.conditions: Death or life imprisonment for abandoning one's post or deserting in the face of the enemy during tactical engagement.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-44.title: Desertion During Mobilization
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-44.conditions: Imprisonment from 7 to 15 years for deserting military service during proclaimed mobilization or national emergency.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-45.title: Desertion in Peacetime
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-45.conditions: Severe confinement from 1 to 5 years for deserting military service in peacetime.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-46.title: Conspiracy and Collective Desertion
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-46.conditions: Imprisonment up to 10 years for collective desertion planned or executed jointly by two or more servicemen.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-47.title: Desertion with Weapons, Aircraft, or Vessels
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-47.conditions: Imprisonment from 7 to 15 years for deserting military duty while carrying military weapons, combat vehicles, or aircraft.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-48.title: Absence Without Official Leave (AWOL)
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-48.conditions: Confinement up to 3 years for unauthorized absence exceeding 15 days in peace or 5 days during mobilization.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-49.title: Concealing and Assisting Military Deserters
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-49.conditions: Confinement up to 2 years for knowingly harboring, concealing, or aiding a military deserter to evade arrest.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-50.title: Intentional Self-Mutilation and Malingering
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-50.conditions: Imprisonment up to 7 years for intentionally inflicting self-mutilation, inducing disease, or malingering to evade military obligations.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-51.title: Assaulting a Military Superior on Duty
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-51.conditions: Imprisonment up to 7 years for physically assaulting a military superior in the execution of his duty or because of his status.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-52.title: Aggravated Assault Causing Death of Superior
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-52.conditions: Death or life imprisonment if physical assault upon a military superior results in death or permanent bodily infirmity.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-53.title: Threatening Superiors with Weapons
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-53.conditions: Imprisonment from 5 to 10 years for threatening a military superior by brandishing or pointing firearms.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-54.title: Insulting and Defaming Military Superiors
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-54.conditions: Confinement up to 3 years for verbally insulting, defaming, or making threatening gestures toward a military superior.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-55.title: Abuse of Command Authority Against Subordinates
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-55.conditions: Confinement up to 3 years for a superior who abuses command authority by striking or mistreating subordinates unlawfully.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-56.title: Compelling Personnel to Perform Unlawful or Personal Tasks
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-56.conditions: Confinement up to 2 years for ordering or compelling subordinate soldiers to render personal services outside official duties.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-57.title: Brawling and Violent Assault Between Peers
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-57.conditions: Confinement up to 2 years for brawling, mutual violence, or assaulting colleagues of equal rank in uniform or quarters.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-58.title: Failure to Suppress Disorder or Violence Among Troops
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-58.conditions: Confinement up to 1 year for any military superior failing to intervene immediately to quell violent altercations occurring in his presence.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-59.title: Filing Vexatious, Malicious, or Fraudulent Complaints
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-59.conditions: Confinement up to 2 years for knowingly submitting malicious, false, or defamatory accusations against superiors or peers.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-60.title: Bribery, Extortion, and Influence Peddling
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-60.conditions: Imprisonment up to 10 years for soliciting or taking bribes or unlawful benefits for granting leaves, transfers, or duty dispensations.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-61.title: Theft and Embezzlement of Military Arms and Ammunition
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-61.conditions: Imprisonment for not less than 7 years for theft, misappropriation, or embezzlement of statutory arms, ordnance, or munitions.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-62.title: Selling, Pawning, or Illicitly Disposing of Military Arms
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-62.conditions: Imprisonment up to 15 years for selling, pawning, pledging, or disposing of military weapons or ammunition entrusted for service.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-63.title: Negligent Loss or Damage to Weapons and Gear
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-63.conditions: Confinement up to 3 years and financial restitution for negligently losing, damaging, or failing to maintain assigned weapons and equipment.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-64.title: Embezzlement of Military Rations, Fuel, and Funds
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-64.conditions: Imprisonment for not less than 5 years and restitution of double the value for embezzling rations, fuel, medical stores, or army funds.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-65.title: Arson and Destruction of Military Depots
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-65.conditions: Death or life imprisonment for intentionally setting fire to, exploding, or destroying munitions depots or armed forces installations.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-66.title: Negligent Discharge of Explosives and Munitions
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-66.conditions: Imprisonment up to 7 years for causing an explosion or detonation of ammunition depots through criminal negligence or disregard of safety.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-67.title: Unlawful Driving and Misuse of Military Vehicles
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-67.conditions: Confinement up to 1 year and restitution of operational damages for driving military vehicles without authorization or for private uses.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-68.title: Forgery in Military Muster Rolls and Rations Registers
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-68.conditions: Imprisonment for not less than 5 years for falsifying or forging military personnel rolls, pay registers, or ammunition delivery vouchers.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-69.title: Collusion and Accepting Defective Military Gear
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-69.conditions: Imprisonment for not less than 7 years for procurement board members accepting defective weapons, expired rations, or unapproved military supplies.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-70.title: Statutory Restitution to the Defense Treasury
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-70.conditions: The military tribunal shall order mandatory return of stolen or embezzled items and full restitution of damages to the defense treasury.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-71.title: Sleeping on Guard Post Facing the Enemy
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-71.conditions: Death or life imprisonment for a sentry found asleep at his post while facing the enemy or on forward tactical contact lines.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-72.title: Sleeping on Sentry Duty in Peacetime
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-72.conditions: Confinement up to 2 years for a sentry sleeping while on guard watch within military quarters in peacetime.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-73.title: Abandoning Guard Post Without Proper Relief
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-73.conditions: Imprisonment up to 10 years for abandoning a guard post in wartime; severe confinement up to 3 years in peacetime.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-74.title: Intoxication and Drug Use While on Duty
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-74.conditions: Severe confinement up to 5 years for being found intoxicated or under the influence of narcotics while performing military duty or watch.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-75.title: Breaching Prohibited Military Zones and Installations
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-75.conditions: Confinement up to 2 years for unlawfully entering restricted military zones or permitting unauthorized persons into secure installations.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-76.title: Divulging Countersigns and Passwords
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-76.conditions: Imprisonment up to 10 years for disclosing passwords, countersigns, or recognition signals to unauthorized personnel.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-77.title: Tampering with Maps and Tactical Situation Reports
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-77.conditions: Imprisonment for not less than 7 years for intentionally forging, manipulating, or misreporting tactical battle maps or situation reports.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-78.title: Forging Military IDs, Travel Passes, and Movement Orders
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-78.conditions: Imprisonment up to 7 years for counterfeiting military identity cards, vehicle passes, movement orders, or tactical travel permits.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-79.title: Subsidiary Application of General Iraqi Penal Code
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-79.conditions: Provisions of Iraqi Penal Code No. 111 of 1969 as amended apply to all matters and offenses not expressly regulated under this Code.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-80.title: Civil Liability and Restitution Claims
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-80.conditions: Imposition of military penal sanctions does not bar civil tort liability or claims for financial damages brought by aggrieved parties.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-81.title: Repeal of Former Military Penal Legislation
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-81.conditions: Military Penal Code No. 13 of 1940 and all amendments thereto are hereby repealed and replaced by this Code.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-82.title: Issuance of Executive Regulations by Minister of Defense
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-82.conditions: The Minister of Defense is authorized to issue directives and internal regulations to facilitate the enforcement of this Code.

iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-83.title: Effective Date and Gazette Publication
iraqi-military-penal-code-2007-83.conditions: This Code shall enter into force from the date of its publication in the Iraqi Official Gazette (Al-Waqaei Al-Iraqiya) No. 4040 on May 9, 2007.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-1.title: Scope of Application
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-1.conditions: The provisions of this Code apply to all military personnel governed under Military Penal Code No. 19 of 2007 as amended, and to prisoners of war.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-2.title: Composition and Structure of Military Courts

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-3.title: Types of Military Trials (Summary and Non-Summary)

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-4.title: Independence of the Military Judiciary
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-4.conditions: Military judges are independent and subject to no authority in their judicial determinations other than the law and conscience.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-5.title: Territorial and Subject-Matter Jurisdiction
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-5.conditions: Military courts possess subject-matter and territorial jurisdiction over crimes under the Military Penal Code committed by military subjects inside or outside Iraq.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-6.title: Subsidiary Application of General Criminal Procedure
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-6.conditions: Provisions of the General Criminal Procedure Code No. 23 of 1971 as amended apply supplementary to all matters not expressly provided herein.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-7.title: Article 7 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-7.conditions: Every serviceman who gains knowledge of a military crime must immediately inform his direct commanding officer or the military investigator.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-8.title: Article 8 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-8.conditions: In unnatural deaths, suspected homicides, or suicides within military units, the commander and investigator inspect the locus and order an autopsy.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-9.title: Article 9 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-9.conditions: Military investigative and intelligence officers exercise judicial police powers to secure crime scenes, preserve evidence, and seize exhibits.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-10.title: Article 10 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-10.conditions: The commanding officer forms a 3-officer Investigative Board chaired by the senior officer to establish facts, examine witnesses, and recommend action.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-11.title: Article 11 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-11.conditions: The accused serviceman must be informed of the charges at the outset of interrogation and possesses the right to remain silent without prejudice.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-12.title: Article 12 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-12.conditions: The accused has the right to legal counsel during preliminary investigations in felony cases; appointed counsel is designated if unrepresented.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-13.title: Article 13 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-13.conditions: Physical and psychological torture and coercion are strictly prohibited; confessions obtained under duress or torture are null and void.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-14.title: Article 14 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-14.conditions: Depositions of witnesses and technical military experts are recorded under oath before the investigator and signed into the official record.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-15.title: Article 15 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-15.conditions: Search of a serviceman's residence or personal quarters requires a judicial search warrant issued by the competent military judge.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-16.title: Article 16 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-16.conditions: Seized weapons and material evidence are labeled, cataloged, attached to the dossier, and lodged in the evidence locker of the court.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-17.title: Article 17 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-17.conditions: The investigator may order medical examinations of the accused or victim to verify injuries, intoxication, or toxicology.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-18.title: Article 18 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-18.conditions: The Military Public Prosecution oversees the legality of the investigation, attends interrogations, and lodges appropriate petitions.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-19.title: Article 19 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-19.conditions: Investigation deadlines may be extended during combat operations by a reasoned decision of the military judge if battles preclude timely completion.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-20.title: Article 20 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-20.conditions: The investigator may conduct confrontational examinations between co-defendants or witnesses to resolve evidentiary discrepancies.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-21.title: Article 21 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-21.conditions: The preliminary investigation closes by judicial order either dismissing the charge for lack of evidence or referring the defendant to trial.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-22.title: Article 22 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-22.conditions: In multi-unit jurisdictional conflicts, the Military Justice Directorate resolves the venue and assigns the competent investigative body.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-23.title: Article 23 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-23.conditions: Military investigative boards may requisition records and official documents directly from civil state ministries and agencies.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-24.title: Article 24 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-24.conditions: Military preliminary investigation proceedings constitute classified defense records; unauthorized leaks trigger severe penal liability.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-25.title: Article 25 - Investigation and Judicial Police Powers
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-25.conditions: Upon conclusion of the investigation, the dossier together with the prosecution's brief is submitted to the referral authority.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-26.title: Article 26 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-26.conditions: An arrest warrant against a military suspect is issued through a reasoned warrant signed by the military judge or referral authority.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-27.title: Article 27 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-27.conditions: Any officer or serviceman may arrest a military suspect caught flagrante delicto (in the act) and deliver him to the nearest command post.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-28.title: Article 28 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-28.conditions: An arrested serviceman must be presented before the military judge within 24 hours of arrest to decide on remand or release.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-29.title: Article 29 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-29.conditions: The military judge may remand the accused for up to 15 days at a time, not exceeding 6 months aggregate except by cassation decree.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-30.title: Article 30 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-30.conditions: Military detainees are held in dedicated garrison remand facilities segregating officers from NCOs and enlisted personnel.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-31.title: Article 31 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-31.conditions: Release on bail or personal surety is permissible for misdemeanors unless detention is required for operational integrity.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-32.title: Article 32 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-32.conditions: Release on bail is strictly prohibited in capital offenses, high treason, and desertion to the enemy.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-33.title: Article 33 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-33.conditions: Military detainees have the statutory right to family contact and confidential visits with their defense attorneys.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-34.title: Article 34 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-34.conditions: Periodic health examinations are conducted for military detainees to verify physical health and investigate abuse allegations.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-35.title: Article 35 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-35.conditions: A detained serviceman receives 50% pay while in custody, retroactively restored in full upon acquittal or dismissal of charges.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-36.title: Article 36 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-36.conditions: A combat field commander may detain an individual endangering unit safety for up to 72 hours before formal judicial arraignment.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-37.title: Article 37 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-37.conditions: Cadets of military academies under detention are remanded within academy quarters under the supervision of the college commandant.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-38.title: Article 38 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-38.conditions: The detainee or defense counsel may appeal detention renewal orders before the competent military court within 3 days.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-39.title: Article 39 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-39.conditions: The military prison commandant bears full legal responsibility for detainee safety and protection against degrading treatment.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-40.title: Article 40 - Military Arrest, Custody, and Bail Protocols
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-40.conditions: The detainee must be released immediately by judicial order if evidence is insufficient to sustain the charge.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-41.title: Article 41 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-41.conditions: Referral powers reside in the Minister of Defense, Chief of Staff, and Division Commanders as prescribed by military directives.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-42.title: Article 42 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-42.conditions: A formal referral decision must set forth the defendant's identity, rank, unit, concise factual charge, penal statute, and trial venue.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-43.title: Article 43 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-43.conditions: Minor infractions are referred by commanding officers to the Disciplinary Officer's Court for prompt summary adjudication.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-44.title: Article 44 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-44.conditions: Felonies and grave misdemeanors carrying custodial sentences are referred to the competent standing Military Court.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-45.title: Article 45 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-45.conditions: A Joint Military Court is formed by judicial decree where civilians and military personnel jointly commit offenses against armed forces security.

iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-46.title: Article 46 - Referral Authorities and Court Transmission
iraqi-military-procedure-code-2016-46.conditions: The referral authority, upon prosecutorial recommendation, may file away proceedings if the act is non-criminal or the accused lacks capacity.
